newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teacher suspended over Dirty War charges.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teacher suspended over Dirty War charges.

text.p: An Argentine high school teacher, accused of working for a police right-wing death squad, has been suspended over allegations of involvement in the 1976 kidnapping and murder of protesting schoolchildren, education officials said on Thursday.

The episode known as "the Night of the Pencils" occurred six months after a military junta took power and declared war against suspected leftists. Up to 30,000 people were reported to have "disappeared" in Argentina during military rule from 1976 to 1983.

Among the Dirty War victims were 11 high school students snatched from their homes in La Plata, capital of Buenos Aires province, on Sept. 16, 1976 for demanding cheap public transport for schoolchildren. Nine were never seen again, two survived.

Education officials said Dr Ernesto Domenech was suspended as head of languages at La Plata's Alberto Thomas Technical School after human rights groups including Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, made up of relatives of the "disappeared", accused him of involvement in the Sept. 16 kidnapping.
"Beroch has been suspended on full pay while the courts carry out their investigations," Claudio Gomez at the province's education department told Reuters.

Provincial Education Secretary Graciela Giannettasio, who has made Sept. 16 a school holiday in the province, issued a statement on Thursday "condemning that horrific episode" and saying: "I want what everybody wants: punishment for the guilty."

Rights groups base their allegations against Beroch on evidence given by a non-commissioned army officer to the 1984 commission set up after the return of democracy to investigate Dirty War crimes. He named Beroch as a right-wing extremist who worked for a police death squad -- charges the teacher denies.
Beroch, 53, said his accusers were "using the same methods as the people who led the military dictatorship. They don't allow for defence. They have just destroyed a person."
